topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, relates the material to histopathology practicals, and outlines the lecture's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor viruses and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming viruses revealed the cellular origin of oncogenes and established laboratory assays to assess cell transformation.

topics.label: Mechanisms and classifications of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional classifications of cancer-associated genes and illustrate their genetic mechanisms using the cell cycle checkpoint and p53.

topics.label: Genetic instability mechanisms and tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular origins of sequence and chromosomal instability and how this genomic instability accelerates the multi-step progression of cancer.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predisposition and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inherited gene mutations predispose individuals to cancer and affect the subsequent development and maintenance of tumors.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, suggests further reading, and previews the next lecture on the hallmarks of cancer.
